clinician.final_diagnosis: the patient was admitted to the surgical service for the management of a liver abscess, presumed to be secondary to perforation of the stomach by an ingested foreign body
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old male presented with 5 days of fever and headache, febrile at 38.2°C, tachycardic and hypertensive, with leukocytosis (12,600/mm3) and mild elevation of liver enzymes (AST 48, ALT 83). Initial chest X-ray was unremarkable except mild right hemidiaphragm elevation. After discharge, the patient returned 3 days later with abdominal tenderness localized to the right upper quadrant and epigastrium. Repeat labs showed worsening leukocytosis (16,500/mm3) and elevated transaminases (AST 52, ALT 105). Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a 5.1 × 7.5 × 3.9 cm heterogenous hypoattenuating lesion in the left hepatic lobe contiguous with the lesser curvature of the stomach at the gastro-hepatic recess, consistent with a liver abscess. Abscess cultures grew Streptococcus anginosus and Actinomyces odontolyticus. The patient was subsequently admitted to surgery for management of the liver abscess, presumed secondary to stomach perforation by an ingested foreign body, although explicit operative findings documenting stomach perforation and foreign body were not provided.

Laboratory values showed increasing leukocytosis and transaminases on readmission
Microbiological culture of abscess fluid grew Streptococcus anginosus and Actinomyces odontolyticus
